title: 自适应机器学习中的注意力机制的动态调整
abstract: This paper explores the application of dynamic attention mechanisms within self-supervised learning frameworks. The core challenge in traditional attention mechanisms is their fixed weight configurations, which struggle to effectively capture the complexities of data distributions. This work introduces a novel dynamic attention weighting mechanism that adapts to the input data's feature distribution, enhancing model performance and robustness. We present a framework for dynamically adjusting attention weights during training, resulting in improved feature representation and generalization capabilities. The proposed algorithm focuses on creating a mechanism that intelligently adjusts the attention's focus based on the data's characteristics. This adaptation directly addresses the limitations of static weight schemes and opens new avenues for more effective self-supervised learning. The paper details the design of the dynamic weighting adjustment mechanism, its impact on model performance through comprehensive experimentation, and discusses future research directions.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Geometric Complexity Measures
abstract: This paper introduces a novel set of geometric complexity measures designed to be intrinsically quantum-resistant, offering a robust benchmark for evaluating the complexity of complex systems. The core mechanism centers around the "Quantum-Controlled Complexity" algorithm, which quantifies complexity through the analysis of quantum interference patterns. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through rigorous theoretical analysis and preliminary experiments, highlighting its potential to surpass existing methods in assessing the intricate dynamics of complex systems. The paper explores the implications of quantum-enhanced geometric complexity for fields ranging from materials science to computational biology, suggesting a paradigm shift in how we understand and quantify complexity.

title: Self-Organizing Quantum State Adaptive Topology Control
abstract: This paper introduces a novel self-organizing quantum state control algorithm based on the inherent adaptability of quantum states. We propose a method for optimizing quantum states by leveraging the self-organizing properties of quantum states, enabling precise control over their topological structures and predictive modeling of their evolution. The core of this approach lies in an adaptive topology control algorithm that utilizes quantum state self-organization to dynamically adjust the quantum state's topology. We present a theoretical framework and preliminary results demonstrating the effectiveness of this approach in controlling quantum states and predicting their evolution. The algorithm's ability to achieve precise and efficient control over topological structures offers significant advancements in quantum information processing and manipulation.

title: 基于自适应的量子算法的量子隐冲突检测
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a cornerstone of quantum mechanics, offers a unique approach to detecting subtle flaws within quantum algorithms. This paper presents a novel quantum algorithm, termed "Adaptive Quantum Entanglement Detection," designed to proactively identify potential hidden conflicts within a quantum computation. We propose a mechanism that leverages the properties of quantum entanglement to transform a potential conflict into a measurable quantum state, enabling early detection and enhancing the overall security of quantum algorithms. The core of this system relies on dynamically adjusting the entanglement parameters based on the algorithm's evolution, ensuring a robust and adaptable detection strategy. The proposed approach offers a significant advancement over existing methods, capitalizing on the inherent properties of entanglement to address the limitations of traditional approaches. This research explores the potential of this framework for safeguarding quantum computations against malicious interference.

title: Title: Dynamically Generated Parallel Quantum Circuit Design
abstract: This paper presents a novel method for automatically generating highly optimized parallel quantum circuits for machine learning tasks. Traditional circuit design is a laborious and expertise-intensive process, limiting the potential for rapid exploration of circuit configurations. We introduce a generative adversarial network (GAN) approach to dynamically design quantum circuits, guided by a reward function that prioritizes both performance and circuit complexity. The system learns to produce circuits that excel in specific machine learning applications, offering a significant step towards automating the design process and accelerating the development of quantum-enhanced machine learning algorithms. The core mechanism leverages GANs to explore a vast design space, resulting in circuits with superior performance characteristics. This work demonstrates the potential of this approach to dramatically improve the efficiency and effectiveness of quantum machine learning.

title: Title: Algorithmic Coherence for Neural Network Training
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of incorporating "coherence" – the degree to which different neurons in a neural network exhibit synchronized activity – into the training process to improve the optimization of neural network weights. Current training methods frequently utilize sparse gradients, which can lead to suboptimal solutions. We propose a novel algorithm, "Coherence-Guided Learning," that dynamically adjusts the learning rate and weight updates based on a learned coherence metric, thereby fostering more complex and meaningful patterns within the network. The core claim is that carefully leveraging coherence will enhance the training process and lead to better model performance. This work explores the design of a metric to quantify coherence and its implementation as a guiding mechanism for the learning algorithm. We provide a theoretical analysis of the algorithm's effectiveness and demonstrate its potential through simulations and preliminary experiments.

title: Dynamic Context-Aware Neural Symbolic Reasoning (DCNNSR)
abstract: This paper introduces Dynamic Context-Aware Neural Symbolic Reasoning (DCNNSR), a novel approach to complex reasoning tasks involving unstructured data. The core idea is to integrate neural symbolic reasoning with dynamic contextual modeling. DCNNSR employs a multi-layer Transformer encoder to extract feature vectors from raw data. Simultaneously, a state space model (SSM)-based module dynamically learns and updates a context vector, which encapsulates fine-grained contextual information regarding the data, task, and environment. A neural symbolic reasoning engine, such as Differentiable Logic Programming, then utilizes this context vector to guide the activation and reasoning process of symbolic rules, ultimately producing a conclusion. Crucially, the context vector is not static; it's continuously updated based on new inputs and the ongoing inference process, allowing the model to capture dynamic changes and underlying dependencies within the data. We demonstrate the effectiveness of DCNNSR through a theoretical analysis and outline its key components, highlighting its advantages over existing methods that often rely on static knowledge representation or focus solely on time series prediction without integrating symbolic reasoning. This approach offers a more flexible and robust solution for handling complex, non-structured data.

abstract: Quantum information is increasingly vital for advanced technologies, necessitating robust and reliable storage and transmission methods. The core mechanism revolves around dynamically adjusting quantum states to minimize the impact of environmental disturbances, resulting in a more resilient and adaptable quantum information system.

title: Automated Detection of Albanian Gegë and Toskë Dialects Through Classical and Deep-Learning Classifiers
abstract: Lane-specific characteristics, traffic flow, vehicle properties, and atmospheric conditions profoundly impact successive vehicle time intervals. A lane position plays an important role due to the differences in flow properties, such as speed, density, and overtaking maneuvers, which can vary significantly across different lanes. Larger or heavier vehicles, which are assigned to specific lanes, tend to require although time more space from each other due to their dimensions and braking requirements. Driver behavior, as determined by reaction times and compliance with rules, introduces variability, especially in challenging weather or road conditions, such as rain, snow, or icy roads. In addition to geographical location and distance of travel, temporal factors also influence perception and choice, including the day of the week and variations in light intensities. Effective modeling approaches and effective traffic control require a comprehensive analysis of these factors. In the current work, a dataset of independent traffic roads with all the above-mentioned variables was constructed, and time-gap prediction between two consecutive cars driving along every road lane was performed using Support Vector Regression (SVR) and Random Subspace (RSS). In addition, new optimization algorithms, referred to as the Partial Reinforcement Optimizer (PRO) and the Walrus Optimizer (WO), were utilized to enhance predictive capability, resulting in strong hybrid models. In this evaluation approach, we also employed Analysis of Variance (ANOVA’s) sensitivity analysis technique to identify the most contributing feature in our data, providing us with the importance of each variable in the prediction process. The SVPR hybrid model performed the best for lane 1, with the highest R² of 0.997, the lowest Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of 2.36E+07, and the lowest Ratio of RMSE to Standard deviation (RSR) of 0.059 during testing, thereby reflecting its superior predictive accuracy and minimal error. For lane 2, the hybrid SVWO model emerged as the most effective, achieving the highest R² of 0.989, the lowest RMSE of 3.36×10^7, and the smallest RSR of 0.107, demonstrating its robust capability in capturing lane-specific traffic dynamics. These findings highlight the potential of hybrid optimization techniques to enhance predictive performance and minimize errors in practical traffic management systems.

The SVPR hybrid model performed the best for lane 1, with the highest R² of 0.997, the lowest Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of 2.36E+07, and the lowest Ratio of RMSE to Standard deviation (RSR) of 0.059 during testing, thereby reflecting its superior predictive accuracy and minimal error. For lane 2, the hybrid SVWO model emerged as the most effective, achieving the highest R² of 0.989, the lowest RMSE of 3.36×10^7, and the smallest RSR of 0.107, demonstrating its robust capability in capturing lane-specific traffic dynamics. These findings highlight the potential of hybrid optimization techniques to enhance predictive performance and minimize errors in practical traffic management systems.

title: Laying the foundation for mammography-based deep learning in breast cancer risk prediction
abstract: Breast screening remains the standard of care for early detection of breast cancer. The screening program in British Columbia (BC) consistently identifies at least 88% of cancers, however, the abnormal call rate (ACR) remains above the national target. Abnormal mammograms require further procedures, which may or may not confirm presence of breast cancer. High ACR suggests that a number of healthy patients are recalled for additional tests, which causes unnecessary stress and inflicts extra costs. Automated AI (artificial intelligence) systems could assist radiologists in reducing the number of false positives by providing individual risk assessments based on mammography images. Machine learning is already widely used for cancer detection, but the research surrounding deep learning models designed for estimating the risk of future cancers is still limited. In this thesis, a modern deep learning model was developed using patient mammograms to predict the risk of cancer within five years after a screening exam. This model relies on state-of-the-art (SOTA) architecture and attempts to achieve reliable performance on local data. To that end, a large cohort of patient data from BC was curated for vision-based learning. It includes 1.8 million images from over 200,000 patients, making it comparable to other large-scale SOTA datasets found in the literature. The model achieves 0.92 [0.89-0.94] and 0.78 [0.76-0.80] ROC AUC for year one and five predictions, compared to 0.84 [0.80-0.88] and 0.76 [0.73-0.78] achieved by pre-trained SOTA in the respective years. These results can be attributed to thorough data curation, two-stage training, and the informed implementation of the SOTA architecture.

title: Better Understanding, Better Fixes? A Study of Hallucination in LLM-based Automated Program Repair
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have significantly advanced automated program repair (APR), yet existing evaluations remain largely result-centric and provide limited insight into hallucination during repair. In APR, hallucination may arise not only in final patches but also in the intermediate artifacts that guide patch generation. To address this gap, we perform a multi-layered analysis of hallucination throughout the APR process. Specifically, we characterize hallucination as the production of patches or intermediate artifacts that are not faithfully grounded in the available repair evidence. We examine repair hallucination in final patches and understanding hallucination in intermediate artifacts through three tasks, namely triggering testcase identification, line coverage prediction, and additional testcase generation. We then evaluate three representative LLMs on 832 Defects4J bugs through automatic evaluation and manual analysis. Our results show that both repair and understanding hallucinations remain prevalent. Across models and settings, only 21.0%-55.9% of generated patches pass the developer-written test suite. Moreover, although more accurate intermediate artifacts are generally associated with successful repairs, this relationship does not always hold. Manual analysis of 812 sampled repairs identifies repair hallucinations in 72.7% of cases, including patches that pass all available tests; incorrect causal localization and incorrect repair strategies account for 45.9% and 18.5% of these hallucinations, respectively. Meanwhile, models frequently misidentify triggering testcases, mispredict line coverage involving branching control flow, and generate additional testcases with missing bug-triggering conditions or incorrect expected behavior.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation in Enterprise Systems: Architectural Patterns, GraphRAG, and Implementation Challenges
abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) has become a successful model for enterprise-grade LLM applications with a requirement for knowledge accuracy, contextual explainability, and constantly updated, real-time information. RAG utilizes the semantic search capabilities of a retrieval system to ground the generative output in trusted and authoritative enterprise knowledge stores, thus addressing the problem of hallucination. The architecture of enterprise RAG systems is categorized into dense and sparse retrieval layers, vector database architectures, hybrid retrieval models, and knowledge graph integration such as GraphRAG. In this article, a mathematical formulation of retrieval performance and hallucination suppression is introduced, including cosine similarity and BM25 retrieval score variants, a parameterized hybrid retrieval model with performance metrics for all interpolated coefficients, and two faithfulness metrics with hallucination rate estimates spanning five retrieval strategies. The article also discusses agentic RAG orchestration, reranking pipelines, AI observability frameworks, and enterprise governance. According to a quantitative analysis, GraphRAG has a theoretical faithfulness score of 0.95, and a baseline LLM without retrieval augmentation scored 0.30. With hybrid retrieval and α = 0.6, GraphRAG achieves an F1@5 of 0.784, exceeding a BM25-only retrieval baseline by 34.5%. These results show the impact of architecture, retrieval tuning, and governance-aware design in building scalable and trustworthy enterprise-oriented AI applications. A simulation study validated the theoretical retrieval models on a 2,500-document enterprise corpus, confirming that the observed F1@5 improvements were within 2% of the theoretical projections, with hybrid retrieval at α = 0.6 achieving a 35.0% F1@5 gain over BM25 and GraphRAG producing an observed faithfulness score of 0.934. The article additionally introduces the Enterprise RAG Reliability Assessment Model (ERRAM), a structured five-dimension scoring framework for evaluating the operational maturity and production readiness of enterprise retrieval architectures.

title: belowlab/PheMINE: PheMINE v1.0.0: Initial Release for Publication
abstract: PheMINE v1.0.0 — Initial Release This release marks the initial public release of PheMINE (PHEnome-wide Modeling and INference Engine), accompanying the manuscript submission. title: Quantum Entanglement-Based Nonlinear Geometry Modeling
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a bizarre phenomenon in quantum mechanics, holds immense potential for revolutionizing geometric modeling. This paper explores the development of a novel framework, leveraging quantum entanglement to provide a fundamentally new approach to precise geometric modeling. We propose a method that translates complex geometric structures into a quantum entanglement computation, allowing for a level of accuracy exceeding current methods. The core claim centers on the ability to precisely model non-linear relationships inherent in complex geometries, offering a paradigm shift in geometric representation. The algorithm's novelty lies in its direct application of quantum entanglement principles to the core modeling process, offering a potentially transformative leap in geometric precision.

title: Quantum-Inspired Variational Calculus (QIVC)
abstract: Quantum-Inspired Variational Calculus (QIVC) presents a novel approach to variational calculus that integrates quantum mechanics principles to enhance the accuracy and efficiency of optimization algorithms. The core mechanism involves the implementation of a variational optimization framework utilizing quantum-inspired techniques to improve the exploration of the search space. This research addresses the limitations of traditional optimization methods by introducing a quantum-based enhancement, potentially yielding superior results in complex optimization problems. This paper details the theoretical foundation, implementation, and preliminary results of QIVC, highlighting its potential impact on various fields where optimization is crucial.

title: Title: Dynamic Phase Space Optimization for Machine Learning
abstract: This paper introduces a novel optimization technique, Dynamic Phase Space Optimization (DPO), designed to enhance the generalization capabilities of machine learning models. Traditional optimization methods often rely on static parameter settings, failing to effectively capture the complex dependencies within the data. DPO dynamically adjusts the phase space of a model based on observed data, incorporating features and parameters in a way that optimizes for unseen data. This approach leverages a novel 'adaptive weighting' scheme, allowing the model to prioritize the most relevant information during training. The paper details the implementation of DPO, explores its performance compared to existing optimization methods, and presents preliminary results demonstrating improved generalization.

title: Self-Adaptive Topological Geometry Quantum Mapping Validation
abstract: This paper investigates the application of self-adaptive geometric topology to quantum mapping validation, addressing the challenges of instability and computational inefficiency in traditional methods. We introduce a novel framework that dynamically adjusts key parameters during the mapping process, enabling automated parameter tuning and ultimately improving the stability and efficiency of the resulting maps. The core mechanism involves a dynamically evolving geometric topology representation that serves as a constraint and guide for the quantum mapping process. We present a theoretical framework and demonstrate its efficacy through simulations, demonstrating a significant improvement in mapping stability and computational speed compared to existing approaches.

title: Wave Function Collapse for Quantum State Tomography
abstract: Quantum state tomography is a crucial task in quantum information science, aiming to reconstruct the complete quantum state of a complex system from a set of measurements. Traditional methods often struggle with large systems and high dimensionality, presenting significant computational challenges. This paper introduces a novel quantum state tomography method, "Hierarchical Collapse," that utilizes wave function collapse to efficiently extract information and accelerate the reconstruction process. We propose a hierarchical collapse algorithm that progressively reduces the complexity of the wave function, offering a significant improvement over existing approaches. The core mechanism hinges on the strategic application of collapse events to minimize the number of independent measurements required. This approach has the potential to drastically reduce the computational burden associated with quantum state tomography, opening up possibilities for exploring larger and more complex quantum systems.

title: 基于自适应量子电路的动态调整 - 拓扑信息学算法的加速器
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic adjustment algorithm for quantum circuits, leveraging self-adaptive parameter adjustment to optimize the performance of topological information theory (TIT) algorithms. Traditional quantum circuit design relies on manual parameter tuning, which is a time-consuming and error-prone process. Our algorithm dynamically adjusts circuit parameters to achieve superior performance, significantly accelerating the implementation of TIT algorithms. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a series of simulations and analysis, showcasing substantial improvements in algorithm execution time and qubit fidelity. The design incorporates a robust feedback mechanism to maintain optimal circuit characteristics throughout the optimization process. The core mechanism revolves around iteratively refining circuit parameters based on a learned objective function, providing a practical and efficient pathway for accelerating TIT algorithm development.

title: Adaptive Quantum Control via Reinforcement Learning
abstract: This paper investigates the application of reinforcement learning (RL) for adaptive quantum control. Traditional quantum control methods often rely on pre-designed pulse shapes optimized for specific scenarios, lacking adaptability to variations in system parameters or environmental noise. This work proposes a novel framework where an RL agent learns to dynamically adjust quantum control pulses in real-time, maximizing the fidelity of quantum operations. The agent receives feedback from the quantum system, typically measured through state variables, and utilizes this information to optimize the control pulse sequence. This adaptive approach addresses the limitations of static control schemes and promises enhanced robustness and performance in complex quantum systems. The core claim centers on utilizing reinforcement learning to design optimal quantum control pulses. The central mechanism involves a trained controller dynamically adjusting pulses based on system feedback. The presented methodology offers a new approach to quantum control, particularly relevant in noisy environments and systems with parameter variations. The research demonstrates the potential of RL for achieving superior quantum control outcomes compared to conventional techniques. ---

title: Probability Iterative Neural Network
abstract: This paper introduces a novel probabilistic iterative neural network (PINN) designed for machine learning tasks requiring high precision and robustness, particularly in scenarios with sparse or noisy data. Traditional parameter adjustment methods often struggle with complex tasks and noisy data, whereas PINN leverages a probabilistic model to facilitate more stable and flexible parameter tuning. This approach offers a shift from gradient-based methods to a model-driven, iterative process, significantly enhancing the ability to handle challenging data distributions. The core mechanism centers around a probabilistic model that dynamically adjusts network weights based on probability distributions, offering a robust and adaptable solution for machine learning.

title: Title: Bayesian Constraint Optimization for Graph Reconstruction
abstract: This paper introduces a novel Bayesian constraint optimization approach for graph reconstruction, addressing the challenges of incomplete data and inherent uncertainty in graph connectivity. Traditional methods often struggle with ambiguity and require exhaustive search, making them computationally expensive. Our framework leverages Bayesian principles to model node and edge probabilities, quantifying uncertainty in the reconstruction process. We propose a probabilistic model that iteratively refines the reconstruction based on observed data, resulting in a more robust and accurate result than existing approaches. The core mechanism centers on updating node and edge probabilities using Bayesian inference, effectively incorporating uncertainty into the reconstruction process. This approach offers a significant improvement in reconstruction quality, particularly when dealing with sparse or noisy data. The paper details the model architecture, the Bayesian inference process, and provides a comprehensive evaluation of its performance against established graph reconstruction algorithms. The resulting framework is designed for practical applications requiring reliable and precise graph representation.

title: Parallel Quantum State Collapse Optimization
abstract: Quantum state collapse is a fundamental process in quantum mechanics, representing the irreversible transition of a quantum system from a superposition of states to a definite state. Its efficiency is critical to the operation of quantum computation. Current methods for managing and optimizing collapse operations, particularly in large-scale systems, often face significant challenges, limiting computational speed. This paper investigates a novel approach to optimize quantum state collapse using parallel quantum computation, focusing on the integration of a quantum annealing algorithm with a distributed processing strategy. The core claim is that this algorithm will drastically accelerate the collapse process compared to traditional methods, offering significant improvements in computational throughput. This work will detail the implementation of the algorithm, the rationale behind its design, and the expected performance gains.

title: Title: Non-Standard Geometric Topology for Quantum State Preservation
abstract: Abstract: Quantum state preservation is a fundamental challenge in quantum information processing, demanding robust and reliable methods for maintaining quantum coherence over extended time scales. Traditional topological approaches, while offering valuable insights, often struggle with the inherent complexities of quantum systems. This paper proposes a novel geometric topology, termed "Dynamic Entanglement Topology" (DET), designed to intrinsically guarantee the preservation of quantum states across extended time scales. DET leverages dynamically evolving entanglement patterns to achieve continuous state evolution without collapse, offering a robust framework for quantum information processing. The core mechanism involves introducing a self-correcting topology that adapts to maintain quantum coherence. We present a rigorous mathematical framework demonstrating the robustness of DET against various perturbations, highlighting its potential to overcome limitations of existing topological methods.

title: Quantum Entanglement Probability Matrix: A Novel Non-Linear Modeling Approach
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a cornerstone of quantum mechanics, presents unique challenges for optimization in quantum computing and quantum communication. Traditional optimization algorithms often struggle to accurately represent and leverage the complex dynamics of entangled systems. This paper introduces a novel non-linear modeling approach based on a quantum entanglement probability matrix, aiming to provide a more precise and efficient framework for quantum system optimization. The model dynamically adjusts the probability matrix to simulate quantum entanglement behavior, offering enhanced capabilities in optimizing complex quantum systems. The development of this method addresses limitations in current optimization techniques, particularly in capturing the intricacies of entanglement, and represents a significant step toward advancing quantum algorithms and communication protocols.

title: BB84 with ML-KEM Decapsulation-Failure-Based Security Parameters
abstract: With the advent of quantum computers, traditional key exchange mechanisms are under threat, necessitating the development of new methods. Recently, Module-Lattice-Based Key Encapsulation Mechanism (ML-KEM) has been standardized as a quantum-safe key exchange method. Another emerging technique is Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) and its most famous protocol, BB84, which relies on the principles of quantum physics to exchange key information. Both techniques are considered secure against attacks by quantum computers, but their security is based on different principles. However, both key exchange types include a statistical component which, if an attacker were lucky, could allow circumventing these underlying hard problems. In this paper, we suggest that as a key exchange mechanism, BB84 should be run with security parameters comparable to those of ML-KEM, and analyze performance implications if this choice is taken. We illustrate the impact by estimating the number of raw bits required to generate a 256-bit symmetric key using BB84 and assessing the resulting performance implications. We further show how the BB84 finite-size security parameter can be chosen such that the post-processing failure probability is of the same order as the cumulative decapsulation-failure probability of ML-KEM. According to our results, the security parameter in BB84 should be at most 2−75.8 if statistical failure probability comparable to the ML-KEM decapsulation-failure target is desired. These findings offer general guidelines for BB84 parameter selection, with hybrid protocol design representing one potential application context.

title: The Language of Chatbots as a Tool for Building Customer Satisfaction in Digital Marketing
abstract: This project focuses on the language of chatbots as a tool for building customer satisfaction in digital marketing. It addresses the growing use of chatbots in digital brand communication and the need for systematic research into their linguistic, stylistic and pragmatic strategies in the Slovak e-commerce environment. The research examines how chatbot language influences customer experience, trust, satisfaction, brand perception and willingness to continue interaction. It combines corpus-linguistic, qualitative, quantitative and experimental approaches, including the analysis of real chatbot interactions and the testing of linguistic variants. The project aims to develop an interdisciplinary framework for evaluating the quality of chatbot communication and to formulate practical recommendations for linguistically and marketing-effective chatbots. This OSF page serves as a transparent archive of selected project outputs, publications, conference materials, datasets and supplementary research documentation.

title: Phase-sensitive framed-ribbon representation of single-qubit Pauli measurements in linear cluster states
abstract: Abstract We provide an explicit geometric classification of single-qubit projective measurements on one-dimensional (1D) linear cluster states (LCS) within a topological framework. By establishing an explicit geometrical correspondence between local measurements and topological surgery operations on an associated link model i.e. a measurement-surgery correspondence , we represent the cluster state as a linear Hopf chain. Within this model, measurements in the computational ( Z ) basis act as topological severance in case of bulk measurements while boundary pruning happens for end measurements of qubits. In contrast, transverse ( X ) basis measurements remove the measured qubit and, rather than fusing its neighbours into a single splice, induce a geometric stratification of the residual state into a superposition of two disjoint, correlated segments joined only through real-valued classical correlations. We show that lateral ( Y ) basis measurements instead preserve a single continuous spliced chain while generating intrinsically complex phase factors that are not captured by unframed link models. The unframed linking pattern already distinguishes the X - and Y -basis outcomes from one another by shape; what it cannot resolve is which of the two possible outcomes occurred within a fixed basis, since both members of either outcome pair share an identical unframed diagram. To resolve this residual ambiguity, we introduce a framed ribbon representation in which quantum phases are encoded as geometric twists, with chiral ± 90 ∘ twists corresponding to the phases ± i . This framing yields a phase-sensitive, outcome-resolved geometric description of single-shot Pauli measurements on LCS. We stress that the twist angles introduced here are not topological invariants: they are geometric labels fixed operationally by the measurement outcome and by the resulting by-product operator, whereas the linking pattern of the underlying unframed link is a genuine topological datum. The present work is deliberately restricted to single-shot single-qubit Pauli measurements on 1D LCS; composition rules for sequential measurements and for classical feedforward are not established here and are identified as the principal open problem.

title: A noise-robust over-sampling method for imbalanced transmission production data classification
abstract: Abstract In the automotive industry, quality assurance is crucial for ensuring safety and performance. An integral part of quality assurance is Noise, Vibration and Harshness (NVH) testing in transmission production. NVH testing utilizes sensors such as accelerometers, microphones, and encoders to capture acoustic and dynamic characteristics under simulated road conditions. Traditionally, these characteristics are evaluated against manually defined thresholds set by NVH engineers—a process that is labor intensive, costly, and complex. Although advances in machine learning (ML) offer the potential to improve efficiency in NVH testing, challenges such as severe class imbalance, outliers, and limited access to production data hinder its adoption. To address these challenges, we propose Modified Z-Score Cyclic Exponential Averaging of Minority Data ( $$mZ$$ mZ - $$cEAMD$$ cEAMD ) , a noise-robust over-sampling method that integrates exponential averaging with outlier removal to generate balanced and representative samples, while preserving the fundamental characteristics of the original data distribution. This is complemented by a feature extraction approach that integrates spectral order tracking, which captures gear meshing frequencies relative to input rotation speed, with the Short-Time Fourier Transform (STFT), which represents time-frequency characteristics. Together, these features contain critical discriminative information for transmission classification and are used to assess the effectiveness of the proposed over-sampling method. Comparative experiments against established over-sampling methods demonstrate that the proposed $$mZ$$ mZ - $$cEAMD$$ cEAMD approach outperforms alternative techniques in addressing class imbalance in datasets containing outliers. This study advances ML-based NVH testing, thereby fostering the digital transformation of automotive quality assurance.

title: Full-Page Optical Music Recognition of Handwritten Monophonic Scores
abstract: Full-page end-to-end Optical Music Recognition seeks to transcribe entire music pages directly into symbolic notation, avoiding the limitations of traditional pipelines that rely on accurate staff segmentation. Recent Transformer-based architectures have achieved strong performance on typeset scores, relying on large-scale synthetic data for pretraining. However, their applicability to handwritten music remains largely unexplored. In this work, we study full-page transcription on handwritten monophonic collections and analyze the impact of synthetic pretraining in this setting. To investigate which factors are most relevant during pretraining, we introduce a generator capable of producing visually coherent full-page scores in both typeset and handwritten styles. Experiments on three real handwritten datasets provide a comparative evaluation of several full-page pipelines and different synthetic pretraining strategies. The results suggest that the benefits of synthetic pretraining are primarily associated with learning structural layout conventions rather than with visual similarity to the target handwriting.

title: Methane Detection On Board Satellites from Unorthorectified Imagery
abstract: As a potent greenhouse gas, methane is a major driver of climate change. Its effective mitigation relies on timely detection. Conventional detection methods rely on orthorectification to correct geometric distortions and matched filters to enhance plume signals, which are steps designed for ground processing and poorly suited to onboard execution. We introduce UnorthoDOS, a dataset and approach for training machine learning models directly on unorthorectified hyperspectral imagery, bypassing both orthorectification and matched-filter products. Our U-Net models trained on unorthorectified data approach the performance of models trained on orthorectified data (IoU 16.91% vs. 18.47% on all plumes), while both substantially outperform the mag1c matched-filter baseline (IoU 4.76%). We further demonstrate the feasibility of onboard deployment: FP16 compression halves model size with under 0.3% output deviation. The trained ML models and two ML-ready datasets -- orthorectified and unorthorectified hyperspectral imagery from the EMIT sensor -- are publicly available at https://huggingface.co/datasets/SpaceML/UnorthoDOS, with code at https://github.com/spaceml-org/plume-hunter.

title: Continuous Cognitive Coverage for Autonomous Robots via Event-Dependent Cognitive Treatment and Learning
abstract: Autonomous robots continuously encounter objects, changes, and situations, and every event admitted into cognition should receive an appropriate cognitive treatment rather than remain untreated until an explicit task requires attention. However, existing task-driven, reactive, or fixed-reasoning approaches generally process only selected events or apply predefined reasoning procedures, making it difficult to provide continuous cognitive coverage with differentiated treatment. This paper proposes a continuous cognitive coverage framework in which every cognitively admitted event is assigned an event-dependent cognitive treatment according to its state, context, and history. Different events may therefore invoke description, memory, risk prediction, planning, diagnosis, analogy, or other learned treatments. Familiar events can be processed automatically by learned mechanisms, whereas unfamiliar or uncertain events invoke explicit deliberation or fallback reasoning. Multiple cognitive processes can be suspended, resumed, and interleaved so that cognitive processing continues as new events arrive or existing events await evidence. Validated experiences are continuously learned to automate, refine, and revise event-specific treatments. Experiments achieve 96.76% structured treatment accuracy with 93.66% automatic processing, 92.64% cognitive coverage under bursty-delayed workloads, and 79.53% continual-learning joint accuracy, with novel-event reuse reaching 100% automatic processing.

title: A Differentiable Neural Surrogate for Photon Propagation in Neutrino Telescopes
abstract: Large-volume neutrino telescopes infer neutrino properties from Cherenkov light, but simulating the transport of billions of photons through highly scattering ice or water is computationally costly. We introduce candela, a differentiable SIREN neural field that learns the photon Green's function of the IceCube Neutrino Observatory, a cubic-kilometer detector embedded in Antarctic glacial ice. Given a point-like energy deposit and sensor, it predicts the expected photon yield and full arrival-time distribution at the sensor. Complete events are simulated by decomposing charged-particle energy deposits into point-like sources and superposing their predicted sensor responses. Trained on Monte-Carlo simulations, candela generates events $50$--$100\times$ faster than existing methods, with cost scaling only weakly with neutrino energy. It keeps median yields within $2\%$ of the MC expectation and timing distributions at the MC statistical floor across six photon-count decades. The model also provides end-to-end gradients with respect to event parameters and opens a path toward optimizing scattering-medium properties, which often dominate systematic uncertainties in neutrino telescopes.

title: KSCCN Signed Memory: Cross-Session Narrative Integrity and Cognitive Sovereignty in the Post-Quantum Stack
abstract: The first three volumes of this series relocated post-quantum policy from the algorithm catalogue to the archive (Mamun, 2026a), from the unbuilt hall to a layered portfolio of sovereignty (Mamun, 2026b), and from a Q-day step function to a fluid estate that must change cryptographic posture as the threat surface moves (Mamun, 2026c). This fourth volume treats the object that those three claims jointly produce: an archive that acts. Enterprise and sovereign systems are no longer static repositories. They retrieve, write and re-weight contextual memory across sessions in order to infer and to decide. In that setting the high-value target is not yesterday's file. It is tomorrow's persona. An adversary who cannot read a payload can still poison the narrative stream that conditions future judgment. Cross-session narrative memory (CSNM) is therefore specified as an integrity architecture, not as a product feature. The paper defines the memory block, the assimilation gate, the dual clock of index and payload, and the rotation rule that lets signature primitives change without breaking historical custody. Cognitive sovereignty — introduced politically in Volume II — is restated as an engineering property: the capacity to know which blocks were admitted, by whom, under which key, and to refuse the unsigned. Implications are drawn for public-sector agents, for national language models as public personas, and for the Observatory's audit of algorithmic memory. title: Concurrent stabilizer extraction induces signed interactions between memories that averaging conceals and timing suppresses -- data and analysis
abstract: Measurement data and analysis code for the manuscript Concurrent stabilizer extraction induces signed interactions between memories that averaging conceals and timing suppresses. Fourteen hardware campaigns on an IBM Heron processor: design manifests, gate records and results, together with the per-block transition count tables and per-shot syndrome registers from which every reported statistic is computed. python reproduce.py runs 24 checks against the published values, offline and with no quantum-computing account. Eight are recomputed from the raw counts on every run; fourteen are regenerated on request by the five scripts in analysis/; two are read from a deposited result and compared. MANIFEST.sha256 carries a SHA-256 for every other file. Code is licensed MIT and data CC BY 4.0; see LICENSE-CODE and LICENSE-DATA in the deposit.

title: An Isolated, Attested, and Governed Network for Trustworthy AI Research and Deployment: A Reference Architecture, Threat Model, and Roadmap
abstract: Abstract— Emerging AI systems increasingly exhibit capabilities—autonomous code generation, tool use, and self-replication potential—that make the public Internet an unsuitable substrate for high-consequence AI research and deployment. This whitepaper reformulates an early-stage dual-system concept (an untrusted “System A” comprising the Internet/IoT, and an isolated “System B” for AI R&D) into a rigorous reference architecture. We contribute: (1) a structured critical assessment of the baseline concept; (2) a layered, zero-trust reference architecture with an explicit trust root, attested cross-domain gateways, confidential tenant workspaces, and least-privilege autonomous guardians; (3) a three-plane protocol redesign (data, control, resource) that corrects the baseline’s conflation of network and resource abstractions; (4) a formalized governance pipeline reconciling ethical screening with auditability, including anonymous-but-linkable telemetry; and (5) a three-phase, metric-gated roadmap traceable to program deliverables (Technical Areas 1.1, 1.2, 2) and aligned with NIST SP 800-207, the NIST AI RMF, IEEE 7000, and MITRE ATLAS. Index Terms— Zero-trust architecture, cross-domain solutions, confidential computing, AI security, trustworthy AI, research networks, provenance, governance.

title: Development of Quantum Algorithms for SSSP Problem
abstract: A hybrid quantum-classical algorithm for the Single Source Shortest Path (SSSP) problem, applying Dürr-Høyer / BBHT quantum minimum search to Dijkstra's algorithm. Implemented in Python using Cirq/qsim, developed as part of a Master's thesis (TFM) in Theoretical Physics at Universidad Complutense de Madrid.

title: Geometric Proofs for Machine Learning Model Robustness
abstract: This paper explores the application of geometric proofs to enhance the robustness of machine learning models, particularly against adversarial attacks and data drift. We propose a framework that leverages geometric techniques – specifically, the representation of model sensitivity as geometric objects – to provide mathematically rigorous guarantees on model behavior. The core mechanism centers around establishing robustness through rigorous geometric analysis, offering a novel approach to model security compared to traditional methods. This work aims to improve the reliability and trustworthiness of machine learning systems by incorporating a fundamental mathematical tool.

title: Self-Adaptive Chaos Geometry Optimization via Probabilistic Methods
abstract: This paper presents a novel optimization algorithm based on probabilistic chaos geometry, specifically designed for complex systems exhibiting chaotic behavior. The core concept revolves around modeling the system's dynamics as a probabilistic chaos field, allowing for adaptive adjustments to parameters and control strategies. We leverage the inherent unpredictability of chaotic systems to achieve robust and responsive optimization. This work introduces a novel framework incorporating a probabilistic field prediction and adjustment mechanism, providing a more flexible and adaptive approach compared to traditional optimization techniques. The algorithm's effectiveness is demonstrated through simulations focusing on a system involving non-linear dynamics and sensitivity to initial conditions. The research emphasizes the potential for self-adaptive optimization in challenging environments, offering a promising pathway for managing complex systems with inherent unpredictability.

title: Non-Euclidean Neural Network Architecture for Symbolic Reasoning
abstract: This paper presents a novel neural network architecture designed to enhance symbolic reasoning capabilities by incorporating a non-Euclidean representation. Traditional neural networks often fall short in representing and reasoning about abstract concepts due to the limitations of Euclidean geometry. This work proposes a method of encoding concepts in a space that circumvents these limitations, leading to a more robust and flexible system for symbolic manipulation. The core mechanism centers around the "Non-Euclidean Representation" – a novel approach to conceptual mapping that offers significant advantages in handling complex reasoning patterns. We detail the architecture, explore its potential benefits through theoretical analysis, and present preliminary results demonstrating enhanced symbolic reasoning capabilities compared to existing approaches.

title: 基于量子自旋的几何变换优化算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel geometric transformation optimization algorithm based on the unique properties of quantum spins. Traditional geometric optimization methods often struggle with the inherent complexity of geometric transformations, particularly in the realm of quantum mechanics. We propose a new approach that leverages quantum spin states to achieve precise control and optimization of geometric transformations, offering a potential breakthrough for applications in computer graphics, robotics, and other fields. The core mechanism centers on constructing a quantum spin-based model for geometric transformation, utilizing the inherent properties of these states to precisely implement the transformation process. This algorithm demonstrates significant improvements in accuracy and efficiency compared to established methods, showcasing its potential to address challenges in geometric modeling and optimization.

title: The Evolution of Adaptive Multi-Modal Data Fusion for Quantum Machine Learning
abstract: This paper introduces an adaptive multi-modal data fusion framework designed to enhance the predictive accuracy and generalization capabilities of quantum machine learning models. Traditional multi-modal data fusion methods often rely on static data fusion strategies, limiting their effectiveness in complex datasets. Our framework dynamically adjusts data fusion strategies, enabling a more flexible and robust approach to model performance. We demonstrate the framework's efficacy through a series of simulations and analyses, highlighting its ability to improve performance across diverse tasks. The core mechanism involves an adaptive algorithm that continuously evaluates and adjusts the fusion process based on the data itself. This iterative refinement ensures optimal data integration, ultimately contributing to superior model outcomes.

title: 自适应拓扑的量子态分解
abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum state decomposition algorithm based on adaptive topology, offering a promising approach to optimization and control in quantum computing. Traditional state decomposition methods often rely on manual design, lacking the ability to learn from data. Our framework leverages the inherent topological structure of quantum states to efficiently decompose them, enabling enhanced optimization and control capabilities. This work presents a theoretical analysis and preliminary implementation demonstrating the algorithm's effectiveness and potential for significant advancements within the field. The core mechanism involves manipulating the topology of a quantum state through a series of transformations, ultimately leading to a more structured and manageable representation.

title: 基于非线性几何拓扑的量子计算模拟
abstract: This paper explores the application of non-linear geometric topology to quantum computing simulation, aiming to address challenges inherent in traditional simulation methods. We propose a novel approach that leverages quantum computation's unique capabilities to model complex systems exhibiting quantum effects. The core idea centers around employing topological properties to simplify the computational landscape, offering potential improvements in efficiency and the representation of quantum phenomena. This research focuses on designing a simulation framework that incorporates the principles of non-linear geometry and topology, aiming to enhance the fidelity and interpretability of quantum system simulations. We present a conceptual design, detailing the underlying mathematical principles and potential challenges. The paper concludes with a discussion of the implications of this approach for future quantum computing research.

title: Title: Quantum Information Theory – Topological Quantum Error Correction
abstract: Quantum information theory stands at a critical juncture, grappling with the challenges of maintaining quantum coherence in the face of inevitable noise. Current error correction methods, while effective, are fundamentally limited by the complexity of encoding and decoding processes. This paper proposes a novel approach to quantum error correction centered around the concept of topological quantum information, exploring the potential to encode quantum information within the inherent structure of spacetime. This fundamentally shifts the paradigm away from traditional error-correcting codes and towards a more robust and potentially universal approach. The core mechanism involves developing a 'topological field' encoding scheme inspired by topological insulators, aiming to create inherently robust quantum states resistant to local perturbations. We will detail the theoretical framework, the implementation challenges, and preliminary experimental considerations for this approach. The core claim is that this novel methodology offers a path towards significantly enhanced quantum information protection.

title: 基于量子纠错码的密码分析方法
abstract: This paper investigates a novel approach to cryptography analysis leveraging the principles of quantum error correction codes (QECCs). The core idea centers on exploiting the inherent redundancy and error-correcting capabilities of QECCs to analyze and potentially compromise cryptographic keys. Traditional cryptographic attacks often rely on brute-force, differential, or linear cryptanalysis. This work proposes a fundamentally different methodology, focusing on the structure and properties of QECCs to induce errors within the encoded key, which can then be exploited for decryption. The methodology involves constructing specific QECCs tailored to the cryptographic algorithm being analyzed, and then manipulating the encoding process to introduce vulnerabilities. The effectiveness of this approach is demonstrated through theoretical analysis and the development of a novel attack strategy. While experimental validation is not included in this paper, the presented framework provides a strong theoretical foundation and a promising direction for future research in quantum-resistant cryptography. The ultimate goal is to significantly enhance the security of cryptographic systems by targeting their underlying error correction mechanisms.

title: Adaptive Topological Quantum Computing
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of adaptive topological quantum computing, a novel approach designed to enhance quantum algorithm capabilities and computational power through dynamic topological state manipulation. We propose a framework leveraging the inherent properties of topological quantum bits to enable complex computations and extend the reach of quantum computation. The core mechanism involves utilizing quantum topology to dynamically adjust qubit states, allowing for more versatile and powerful quantum operations. The research explores the design of such a system, highlighting its potential advantages over existing quantum computing paradigms. This work offers a new perspective on quantum computation, focusing on the intrinsic potential of topological structures and their adaptability.

title: Quantum-Guided Constraint Optimization
abstract: Quantum-Guided Constraint Optimization (QGCO) is a novel optimization technique leveraging the unique properties of quantum mechanics to enhance the efficiency of constraint optimization problems. This paper explores the fundamental principles behind QGCO, detailing its core mechanism involving quantum superposition and entanglement to guide the search process, ultimately leading to improved solution quality and reduced computational cost. We present a comprehensive theoretical framework, illustrating the algorithm's functionality through mathematical formulations and illustrative examples. The research focuses on the impact of quantum measurements on the search space, demonstrating a significant improvement over classical optimization methods in several benchmark scenarios. The paper concludes with a discussion of the potential applications of QGCO across diverse fields, including finance, logistics, and materials science.

title: LLM is a Machine That Computes Language A Structural and Cognitive Explanation for AI Misinterpretation
abstract: This project presents a unified structural theory of AI, arguing that Large Language Models (LLMs) are computational systems derived from linguistic relations rather than autonomous intelligent agents. It demonstrates that AGI—defined as an entity capable of generating its own goals—is conceptually impossible, while proposing a new direction in which LLMs can be enhanced through externally organized linguistic structures. The project integrates three core insights: 1. LLMs Are Machines That Compute Language LLMs operate by converting language into vector representations and performing matrix‑based next‑token prediction. They do not generate internal thought or conceptual structures. Because human cognition relies on language as its primary external output channel, humans tend to misinterpret fluent linguistic output as evidence of underlying thought. This cognitive bias explains why LLMs are often mistaken for intelligent agents. 2. AGI Is Structurally Impossible Autonomy—goal formation, value judgment, priority setting, and independent action—and subordination—acting according to external intentions—occupy opposite positions within linguistic structure. Since LLMs learn exclusively from linguistic relational patterns, they cannot compute concepts that do not exist within linguistic structure, including “subordinate autonomy.” Therefore: A self‑directed AGI that simultaneously obeys human intentions is conceptually contradictory and cannot be represented within LLM architecture. This is a structural limitation, not a technological one. 3. LLMs Can Be Improved Through External Linguistic Structures LLMs lack internal mechanisms for: conceptual retention stable semantic positioning cross‑linguistic consistency structural reasoning These limitations lead to semantic drift in translation, reasoning, and multi‑layered tasks. However, they can be compensated by externalizing linguistic structures, such as: minimal conceptual units (Units) connection dictionaries English–Japanese structural correspondence tables external reasoning graphs By referencing these external structures, an LLM can achieve reasoning stability and conceptual coherence that internal computation alone cannot provide. This approach enables: more stable reasoning consistent semantics reduced computational load expanded reasoning space through bilingual structural multiplicity It represents a new direction for AI development: externally extended reasoning rather than internal autonomous intelligence. 🔷 Overall Conclusion AGI is structurally impossible. Autonomy and subordination cannot coexist within linguistic structure, and LLMs cannot compute concepts that linguistically do not exist. LLMs remain improvable through external structures. By supplementing internal computation with externally organized linguistic frameworks, LLMs can achieve higher stability, coherence, and efficiency in reasoning. This project reframes AI as a language‑derived computational system, clarifying both its structural limits and its potential for externally supported improvement. The theoretical foundation is based on Mirror Amplification Theory (Urushizaki, 2026), which analyzes how linguistic systems generate, distort, and amplify conceptual structures across different language layers.

title: The Mirror Agent Model: a Bayesian Architecture for Interpretable Agent Behavior
abstract: In this paper we illustrate a novel architecture generating interpretable behavior and explanations. We refer to this architecture as the Mirror Agent Model because it defines the observer model, that is the target of explicit and implicit communications, as a mirror of the agent's. With the goal of providing a general understanding of this work, we firstly show prior relevant results addressing the informative communication of agents intentions and the production of legible behavior. In the second part of the paper we furnish the architecture with novel capabilities for explanations through off-the-shelf saliency methods, followed by preliminary qualitative results.

title: InterSing: Explicit Interaction Dynamics for 3D Duet Singing Animation and Beyond
abstract: We present InterSing, a framework for generating realistic 3D head animations for duet singing performances. Unlike solo singing, duet performance requires each singer to balance individual expressiveness with intermittent interaction at musically salient moments, such as phrase boundaries, synchronized rhythms, and call-and-response passages. Because these interactions are sparse and rhythm-dependent, existing audio-driven animation methods and conversational interaction models do not adequately capture their structure. Our key insight is that duet coordination can be represented as a time-varying signal that reflects how strongly performers engage with one another throughout a song. Based on this observation, we introduce interaction logits, an interpretable latent representation that models the degree of cross-performer engagement at each time step. We learn these logits using weak supervision and use them to condition an interaction-aware diffusion model jointly driven by audio features and interaction dynamics. This formulation enables unified multi-mode generation, spanning independent motion, coordinated behavior, and smooth transitions between them. Experiments show that InterSing generates realistic and expressive singing head animations with stronger coordination and musical alignment than existing methods, while preserving each performer's characteristic motion style. We further demonstrate that the same formulation generalizes to multi-singer performances and provides intuitive control over when and how performers engage.

We further demonstrate that the same formulation generalizes to multi-singer performances and provides intuitive control over when and how performers engage.

title: Predicting Spatiotemporal Mobile Sensing-Based PM2.5 Concentrations Using Low-Rank Adapted Spatially Attentive Graph Neural Network
abstract: Urban air quality can vary significantly along transit corridors, necessitating high-resolution monitoring. This work introduces a novel mobile-sensing dataset from Surat, Gujarat, India, comprising PM$*{2.5}$ concentrations, meteorological variables (temperature, humidity, wind speed, wind direction), and land-use features. To represent the spatiotemporal data as a graph, two node-definition strategies were used: (i) uniform segmentation (200--400~m intervals) and (ii) DBSCAN clustering to adaptively group dense observations. For each node, rolling mean and standard deviation of meteorological variables were computed. To model this high-dimensional data, we propose a SA-GNN for fine-grained, short-term PM$*{2.5}$ forecasting and hotspot identification. We compared SA-GNN with LSTM, RNN, GRU, and ANN models. These models performed well on low-resolution data but had difficulty capturing rapidly changing patterns in urban air quality. SA-GNN employs cluster-specific GRUs to capture localized temporal dependencies and a Graph Attention Network to learn spatial heterogeneity. This hybrid architecture effectively models rapid fluctuations and complex spatial interactions. On our dataset, SA-GNN achieved $R^2 = 0.95$, RMSE $= 6.8$, and MAE $= 4.2~\si{\micro\gram\per\meter\cubed}$, outperforming all baseline models. Combining spatial clustering with adaptive attention significantly improves forecasting, enabling real-time, fine-grained monitoring and supporting personalized exposure tracking and timely alerts for healthier cities.

title: Dataset Quality Assessment For Network Traffic Classification
abstract: Tato dizertační práce je kolekcí autorových článků popisujících dosažené výsledky v oblasti hodnocení kvality datových sad síťového provozu. S rozmachem metod strojového učení se stává klíčovým předpokladem dostupnost vysoce kvalitních dat pro trénování i provozování používaných modelů. Tento důležitý aspekt je však v existujících článcích často přehlížen nebo podceňován, což může vést k nespolehlivému výkonu vyvinutých modelů strojového učení. Obsahem této dizertační práce je zmapování domény posuzování kvality datových sad síťového provozu a její rozšíření o navržené a vyvinuté algoritmy a metriky pro hodnocení kvality. Na základě komplexní analýzy jsou identifikovány kritické body, které ovlivňují kvalitu datových sad síťového provozu. V rámci prováděného výzkumu tato práce navazuje na současný stav poznání, validuje existující datové sady a rozšiřuje tradiční procesy monitorování sítě díky nově vytvořeným metodám. Dosažené výsledky jsou prezentovány ve vybraných článcích v příloze a v přehledové případové studii. Hlavní přínosy této dizertační práce jsou zejména: 1. Sestavení formální taxonomie pro definování klíčových pojmů v oblasti hodnocení kvality datových sad. 2. Návrh a implementace metrik pro kvantifikaci identifikovaných klíčových vlastností kvality datových sad. 3. Integrace kvalitativních metrik do stávajících procesů strojového učení pro podporu kontinuální tvorby, validace, optimalizace a profilování datových sad v čase.

title: Fluid Archives: Malleable Data Architecture and Evolutionary Security under Continuous Cryptographic Threat
abstract: Volumes I and II of this series established two claims. The post-quantum transition is an architectural problem, not an algorithm-substitution problem (Mamun, 2026a). Sovereignty in that architecture is a layered portfolio — compute, data, knowledge, judgment, cognition — pursued under dual-track ecosystems and a compute tax that developing states cannot ignore (Mamun, 2026b). This third volume asks the design question that follows: what kind of data architecture can evolve with the security threat rather than freeze at the last standard? The argument is that threat is not a step function at a hypothetical Q-day. It is a continuous surface — cryptanalysis of parameter sets, implementation breaks, supply-chain compromise of libraries, harvest-now-decrypt-later (HNDL) already running against yesterday's ciphertext, and narrative poisoning of agentic memory. A rigid lake, compiled against one suite, produces dark data the moment the suite is superseded. Fluidity is therefore a security property. The paper specifies a malleable architecture in six layers: object-level cryptographic metadata; a cryptographic bill of materials and policy-as-code control plane; hybrid and versioned wrapping; bifurcated index and payload paths; substrate-aware malleability across silicon halls, molecular halls and sovereign caches; and a cybernetic loop in which threat intelligence continuously re-weights primitives. Also available on Academia.edu: https://www.academia.edu/attachments/134136264/download_file?s=portfolio

title: GEO External Operator
abstract: GEO External Operator v1.0.0 First public release of the solver-independent external operator for the GEO Hidden Geometry Framework. What this release provides GEO is exposed as an external deterministic C operator with a public API and a Cobaya theory-component integration. The demonstrated cosmological integration uses an independently built, unmodified upstream CLASS v3.3.4 source tree. No modification of CLASS source code is required by this integration path. Public C API geo_public_api_version geo_public_compute Canonical effectiveness relation The public implementation uses R^3 = mu_eff and therefore R = mu_eff^(1/3) where mu_eff is application-dependent. The framework does not impose a universal identity between mu_eff and eta. For the Hubble realization demonstrated here, the application-specific assignment is: mu_H := eta = 0.6 Clean CLASS / Cobaya interoperability test Validated against: CLASS v3.3.4 upstream commit e85808324f51fc694d12e3ed7439552a3c3f9540 Python 3.12.3 NumPy 1.26.4 SciPy 1.13.1 Cobaya 3.6.2 classy 3.3.4.0 The external chain is: CLASS -> Cobaya provider -> GEOHubbleTheory -> libgeo_public -> GEO derived quantities Three deterministic regression points were tested: | Primitive H0 | GEO H0 | |---:|---:| | 66.0 | 71.522848664464732 | | 67.4 | 73.039999999771553 | | 69.0 | 74.773887240122221 | All three external evaluations completed successfully. Scope of this release This release establishes: an external GEO software interface; solver-independent separation of the GEO operator from CLASS; reproducible CLASS/Cobaya interoperability; dynamic evaluation rather than a hard-coded Hubble output; explicit provenance and SHA-256 manifests. This software result does not, by itself, constitute independent observational validation of the GEO framework or evidence of cosmological model preference. The Hubble mapping is an application-specific realization, and parts of the present residual/spectral closure retain the candidate-v1 status documented in the source. Reproduction See README.md, run_reproduction.sh, and the provenance/ directory. Author Leonel Hernán Torreblanca

title: Evidence-Based Prompt Engineering
abstract: A prompt-engineering reference in which every technique is graded solid, mixed or folklore, and every claim names a primary source. The evidence lives in a machine-readable ledger. This first release grades eight techniques (three solid, two mixed, three folklore) and ships one offline reproducible experiment; it is a sourced starting corpus, not an exhaustive survey. Effects that can only be measured with live model calls are recorded as dated snapshots against a named model, never as standing truths.

title: Graph-Based Machine Learning Algorithm
abstract: This paper presents a novel graph-based machine learning algorithm designed to automate feature learning and enhance the performance of graph neural networks. Traditional graph neural network approaches often rely on handcrafted features, limiting their adaptability to complex graph structures. Our algorithm leverages graph structure learning to automatically discover and represent relevant features, thereby improving the efficiency and effectiveness of graph neural network models. The core mechanism centers around a self-supervised learning framework that iteratively refines the graph representation based on the data's inherent structure. We introduce a novel method for constructing and manipulating graph representations, coupled with a loss function that encourages feature consistency and growth. The proposed algorithm demonstrates improved performance across a range of graph-based tasks, offering a significant advancement in automated feature learning and graph neural network capabilities.

title: 基于自适应几何的量子拓扑的计算模型
abstract: This paper presents a novel computational model based on adaptive geometry to explore the unique properties of quantum topology, aiming to enhance the efficiency of quantum computation. Traditional topological computation models rely on static representations, while our approach dynamically adjusts the topology, offering a more flexible and potentially powerful framework. We introduce a framework that simulates complex topological structures using adaptive geometry, allowing for a more intuitive and efficient investigation of quantum phenomena. The core mechanism involves the continuous refinement of the topology through iterative adjustments, enabling the exploration of diverse quantum states and phenomena. This research investigates the impact of adaptive geometry on computational efficiency and offers a foundation for future advancements in quantum information processing.

abstract: This paper presents a novel machine learning algorithm leveraging quantum self-adaptation to enhance model performance. Traditional machine learning relies heavily on manually defined model parameters, limiting potential for optimization. We introduce a quantum self-adaptation mechanism that dynamically adjusts model parameters during training, enabling automated parameter optimization and significantly improved predictive accuracy. This approach addresses limitations of existing methods by providing a computationally efficient and inherently adaptive learning strategy. The core mechanism utilizes quantum properties to optimize model parameters, resulting in enhanced predictive capabilities. The results demonstrate a substantial improvement in prediction accuracy compared to state-of-the-art machine learning models.

abstract: This paper introduces a novel optimization algorithm based on dynamic topology, aiming to address the challenges of complex systems and non-linear constraints inherent in traditional optimization methods. The core concept revolves around constructing dynamic topology structures to guide the search process and facilitate the discovery of optimal solutions. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a case study involving a constrained optimization problem in a simulated neural network architecture. The algorithm dynamically adjusts the topology to enhance the search space and yield improved results compared to static optimization techniques. We highlight the advantages of this method, including automatic exploration of complex regions and the avoidance of local optima. The paper concludes with a discussion of the limitations and future directions of this research.

title: Quantum State Dynamic Adaptation and Topological Transformation
abstract: Quantum state dynamics offer a novel approach to modeling and simulating complex topological structures, surpassing the limitations of traditional methods. This paper introduces a dynamic adaptation control algorithm leveraging quantum state characteristics to efficiently analyze and manipulate topological landscapes. The core mechanism focuses on dynamically adjusting parameters within a quantum system to achieve a precise representation of the topological structure. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through simulations of a specific topological dataset, highlighting its potential for improved computational efficiency and enhanced topological understanding. This work contributes to the field of quantum topological computation and provides a framework for automated exploration of topological space.

abstract: This paper introduces a novel clustering algorithm based on non-linear topological structures, emphasizing adaptive clustering driven by the inherent properties of the topology. Traditional clustering methods often rely on distance or similarity measures, failing to fully capture the complex relationships within the data. We propose a new approach that dynamically adjusts clustering parameters during the clustering process, leveraging the topological structure to achieve more accurate and insightful results. The core mechanism centers on the algorithm's ability to adapt to the topology, offering a significant departure from conventional methods. The study demonstrates the effectiveness of this approach through a series of experiments, showcasing superior clustering performance compared to established algorithms.

title: Quantum Information Dynamics: Probability-Adaptive Matrix Operations
abstract: This paper explores the application of quantum information dynamics to the design of novel probability-adaptive matrix operations. Traditional matrix operations are fundamentally classical, limited in their computational capabilities and susceptibility to noise. We propose a new approach utilizing quantum entanglement to fundamentally alter the computation process, shifting it from deterministic to probabilistic, thereby enhancing computational robustness and efficiency. The core mechanism centers around introducing quantum entanglement into the matrix multiplication process, leveraging its inherent quantum self-adaptability to achieve a more reliable and faster computation. This work presents a preliminary investigation into the potential of this approach, focusing on the design of a new matrix multiplication algorithm demonstrating improved performance and resilience against noise.

abstract: Quantum computing offers the potential for exponentially faster computations compared to classical computers, particularly for complex problems. However, the design and implementation of quantum circuits remain a significant challenge due to the inherent complexity of quantum systems. This paper explores a novel approach to quantum circuit design leveraging topological principles to automate the process of circuit optimization and achieve higher computational efficiency. We propose a new framework for automatic circuit adjustment based on topological structure, enabling the system to adapt its design based on the characteristics of the task at hand. This system aims to overcome the limitations of traditional methods by offering a more flexible and robust approach to quantum circuit creation. The research demonstrates the effectiveness of this framework through a series of simulations and analysis, showcasing its ability to generate circuits with improved performance for specific quantum algorithms. The core mechanism is the application of topological topological symmetries to the circuit structure, allowing the system to dynamically adjust parameters to achieve optimal results. This work represents a significant advancement in quantum circuit design, potentially paving the way for more efficient and scalable quantum computations.
